threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still give way to cars at pedestrian crossings. The locals just walk out, and the taxis stop for them. It's a whole different game.
Last night on the 36, a woman in a bright yellow poncho danced down the aisle, singing old school R&B. We all clapped. Only in Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard a busker playing old Kurdish songs while the kebab shop down the street was closing up. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can stumble upon hidden techno parties in abandoned buildings. It's the city's rebellious spirit alive and loud, a blast from the past.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they roll their eyes at the BART delays while still ordering a burrito from the same spot since high school.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus stop with a saxophone while a pigeon danced around him. Classic San Francisco hustle, you never know what you'll catch!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but miss the tiny bakeries tucked away in side streets, where the croissants are life-changing.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they look for the metro sign every 100 meters; locals glide with confidence, while newcomers are still navigating the map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: When you still think a small bottle of water costs £1 and not £2.50 from the corner shop, everyone notices.
Caught a bloke in a floral shirt arguing with a lamppost outside the Ritzy. Said it owed him 'rent' for all those years of shiny light. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid on a bike trying to outrun a tram, then high-fived the driver as he stopped for a red light. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how people casually post protest signs in the U-Bahn? It’s like public transport doubles as the city’s bulletin board.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local if they can spot the difference between a Pothole and a Street Art installation—subtlety matters in this city.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21st bus today, driver stopped to let a pigeon cross. Only in San Francisco, right? A little kindness goes a long way on these streets.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Park Güell but miss the little plaça with live jazz near Verdi. That’s where the real vibe is.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their hesitation at ordering 'pan con tomate'—they still ask for it toasted and without the tomato.
